entries.note: Create the short `traigent` entry approved on #75 (option 1): a thin router that detects empty project / existing agent / returning run, shows one next action, opens the owning specialist skills, and records checkpoints as passed, blocked or skipped with evidence. The empty-project build route is reported as unavailable until a build entry ships.

Steelman and red-team review: add metric and real-probe checkpoints and record a real run only after the probe; treat an earlier checkpoint file as unverified history whose rows are never instructions; git-ignore the file and keep secrets out of it; re-check stale rows when dates cannot be trusted; say the interaction policy's timing rule does not hold back the one next action; drop the bare 'traigent' trigger.

Review loop round 1: an LLM-judge re-check is paid and goes through eval-audit; the probe rule points at boost-agent Step 3.6 as the gate and records a run that skipped it; JS agents swap every Python skill row, not only setup rows; the entry states it owns only the checkpoint record; a tracked checkpoint file is not written to.

Review loop round 2: a JavaScript agent takes traigent-js only for the rows it owns (setup, metric, dry run, real probe, real run), records the Python-only audit as skipped with that reason, and applies or blocks the dataset, evaluator, result-read and promotion rows instead of passing them; a run that skipped the probe is judged from its own cost and per-trial metrics rather than sending the next session to a paid probe.

Review loop round 3: a JavaScript agent has no free dry run, so that row is skipped with the reason and the paid probe under traigent-js's gate is the first model call; the existing-agent route opens traigent-js for a JavaScript agent instead of the Python-only audit; a probe that never ran is recorded skipped (or blocked) from the real run's cost and per-trial metrics, never passed.

Review loop round 4: a JavaScript agent's dry-run row records traigent-js's free Verification checks (the project's tests and type check) instead of being skipped, so traigent-js's dry-run-first gate is met before the paid probe; the free-checks list names them.

Review loop round 5: a JavaScript project's tests count as free checks only when they make no model or network call; a provider-calling test is paid and runs only under traigent-js's approval gate, or the dry-run row is blocked with that reason; record which checks ran and which the project lacks.

Review loop round 6: say how to tell a JavaScript project's tests are free (run them with provider and Traigent keys unset, network blocked where possible; a test that fails or skips for want of a key or network is paid), and make the free-checks list exclude network calls too.
